body:
Sixth sweep: the workspace budget guard, chosen because the certification chain's original p0 was a dense coercion blowing up memory at 50k features, so this is the mechanism that was hardened.

IT WORKS. Budget enforced at every level tested - 1e9 and 1e6 allowed, 1e4, 1e3 and 1 blocked, each with the exact requirement named in bytes. Nonsense budgets refused: -1, 0, NA and Inf all rejected with 'workspace_bytes must be NULL or one positive finite number'. workers > 1 refused with 'workers > 1 is not implemented in effectagram 0.1; workers must be 1', which is one of the five genuinely good messages in the package.

ONE MEASUREMENT WORTH CARRYING ELSEWHERE. Same request, same frame, same pairing:

  materialized   conservative memory plan requires 111360 bytes
  query-first    the same request requires          59300 bytes

47 percent less workspace. So the query-first routing I proposed for the convenience verbs is not only semantically safe - which I verified earlier from R/views.R:269-273 - it is materially cheaper in memory. Noted on bd-01KZYAV8X93BX4VC13Z8PK8XRH. Combined with the earlier timing work the full trade is now measured on both axes: materialized costs more memory and amortizes across questions; query-first costs less memory and pays per question. The one-liner serves the second case, which is the real one when workspace is what binds - which on brain-scale data it is.

ONE DOCUMENTED PROMISE NOT KEPT - bd-01KZYPWMGS0RH11S5ZXQ10MWKV. introduction.Rmd:319-321 says plan construction validates sources, axes, the frame, pairing AND COMPUTE POLICY without reading a neural block. Measured:

  plan_geometry(..., compute = compute_policy(workspace_bytes = 1))   -> plan built
  geometry(that_plan)                                                 -> blocked, 111360 bytes needed

So the compute policy is validated at materialization, not at plan construction. Nothing is broken and no data is touched - the estimate is shape-derived - but the promise names the wrong step. It matters because the whole argument for the plan object is finding out early, and an impossible budget is exactly the error a user would most want caught early. Cheapest fix is to move the estimate into plan_geometry, since it is computed from shapes the plan already holds.

Six sweeps, thirty-four findings. The tally is unchanged in shape: every defect in the surface, every mathematical and statistical claim that I have been able to test holding. This one adds a category I had not previously probed - the safety mechanisms - and they hold too.
